sanskrit: mahātmā cārusarvāṅgaḥ kambugrīvo mahābhujaḥ rukmapṛṣṭhaṃ dhanuḥ khaḍgaṃ tūṇāṃś cāpi parāmṛśat
english: That great-souled one, beautiful in every limb, with a conch-like neck and mighty arms, took up his gold-backed bow, his sword, and his quivers.

sanskrit: kesarīva yathotsiktaḥ prabhinna iva vāraṇaḥ vyapetabhayasaṃmohaḥ śailam abhyapatad balī
english: Like a maned lion in its pride, like a bull elephant in rut, free from fear and confusion, that mighty one rushed toward the mountain.

sanskrit: taṃ mṛgendram ivāyāntaṃ prabhinnam iva vāraṇam dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni bāṇakhaḍgadhanurdharam
english: All beings beheld him coming like the king of beasts, like a raging elephant, bearing arrows, sword, and bow.

sanskrit: draupadyā vardhayan harṣaṃ gadām ādāya pāṇḍavaḥ vyapetabhayasaṃmohaḥ śailarājaṃ samāviśat
english: Gladdening Draupadī's heart, that son of Pāṇḍu took up his mace, and free of fear and bewilderment, entered the king of mountains.

sanskrit: na glānir na ca kātaryaṃ na vaiklavyaṃ na matsaraḥ kadā cij juṣate pārtham ātmajaṃ mātariśvanaḥ
english: Lassitude, cowardice, distress, or envy — none of these ever afflict this son of Pārthā, this son of the Wind-god.

sanskrit: tad ekāyanam āsādya viṣamaṃ bhīmadarśanam bahutālocchrayaṃ śṛṅgam āruroha mahābalaḥ
english: Reaching that single passage, terrible to behold, the mighty one climbed the peak towering with its many tall trees.

sanskrit: sa kiṃnaramahānāgamunigandharvarākṣasān harṣayan parvatasyāgram āsasāda mahābalaḥ
english: Delighting the Kiṃnaras, great Nāgas, sages, Gandharvas, and Rākṣasas, that man of great strength reached the summit of the mountain.

sanskrit: tatra vaiśravaṇāvāsaṃ dadarśa bharatarṣabhaḥ kāñcanaiḥ sphāṭikākārair veśmabhiḥ samalaṃkṛtam
english: There the bull of the Bharatas beheld the abode of Vaiśravaṇa, adorned with mansions of gold fashioned like crystal.

sanskrit: modayan sarvabhūtāni gandhamādanasaṃbhavaḥ sarvagandhavahas tatra mārutaḥ susukho vavau
english: Born on the Gandhamādana, carrying every fragrance, a delightfully pleasant breeze blew there, gladdening all beings.

sanskrit: citrā vividhavarṇābhāś citramañjaridhāriṇaḥ acintyā vividhās tatra drumāḥ paramaśobhanāḥ
english: Wondrous trees of various colors and lustres, bearing variegated blossoms, inconceivable, of many kinds — supremely beautiful — stood there.

sanskrit: ratnajālaparikṣiptaṃ citramālyadharaṃ śivam rākṣasādhipateḥ sthānaṃ dadarśa bharatarṣabhaḥ
english: The bull of the Bharatas beheld the auspicious dwelling of the lord of Rākṣasas, encircled by a net of gems and adorned with garlands of many hues.

sanskrit: gadākhaḍgadhanuṣpāṇiḥ samabhityaktajīvitaḥ bhīmaseno mahābāhus tasthau girir ivācalaḥ
english: Mace, sword, and bow in hand, having cast aside all regard for his life, mighty-armed Bhīmasena stood immovable as a mountain.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaṅkham upādhmāsīd dviṣatāṃ lomaharṣaṇam jyāghoṣatalaghoṣaṃ ca kṛtvā bhūtāny amohayat
english: Then he blew his conch, making the hair of his enemies stand on end; and with the twang of his bowstring and the clap of his palm he confounded all creatures.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃhṛṣṭaromāṇaḥ śabdaṃ tam abhidudruvuḥ yakṣarākṣasagandharvāḥ pāṇḍavasya samīpataḥ
english: Then, their own hair bristling with excitement, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Gandharvas rushed toward the son of Pāṇḍu at that sound.

sanskrit: gadāparighanistriṃśaśaktiśūlaparaśvadhāḥ pragṛhītā vyarocanta yakṣarākṣasabāhubhiḥ
english: Maces, iron clubs, swords, javelins, spears, and battle-axes, gripped in the arms of Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, blazed forth magnificently.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ teṣāṃ tasya ca bhārata taiḥ prayuktān mahākāyaiḥ śaktiśūlaparaśvadhān bhallair bhīmaḥ praciccheda bhīmavegatarais tataḥ
english: Then, O Bhārata, battle commenced between them and him; the javelins, spears, and battle-axes hurled by those huge-bodied ones Bhīma severed with his swift-flying broad-headed arrows.

sanskrit: antarikṣacarāṇāṃ ca bhūmiṣṭhānāṃ ca garjatām śarair vivyādha gātrāṇi rākṣasānāṃ mahābalaḥ
english: That man of great strength pierced with his arrows the bodies of those Rākṣasas who roared as they moved through the sky and stood upon the earth.

sanskrit: sā lohitamahāvṛṣṭir abhyavarṣan mahābalam kāyebhyaḥ pracyutā dhārā rākṣasānāṃ samantataḥ
english: That great rain of blood poured down upon that mighty hero — streams of it flowing from the bodies of Rākṣasas all around.

sanskrit: bhīmabāhubalotsṛṣṭair bahudhā yakṣarakṣasām vinikṛttāny adṛśyanta śarīrāṇi śirāṃsi ca
english: Cut asunder in many ways by arrows released through the strength of Bhīma's arms, the bodies and severed heads of Yakṣas and Rākṣasas were seen everywhere.

sanskrit: pracchādyamānaṃ rakṣobhiḥ pāṇḍavaṃ priyadarśanam dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni sūryam abhragaṇair iva
english: All beings watched that fair-looking son of Pāṇḍu being overwhelmed by the Rākṣasas, even as the sun is obscured by masses of clouds.

sanskrit: sa raśmibhir ivādityaḥ śarair arinighātibhiḥ sarvān ārchan mahābāhur balavān satyavikramaḥ
english: Like the sun with its rays, that mighty-armed and truly valiant hero of great strength struck down all of them with his enemy-slaying arrows.

sanskrit: abhitarjayamānāś ca ruvantaś ca mahāravān na mohaṃ bhīmasenasya dadṛśuḥ sarvarākṣasāḥ
english: Though they threatened him and roared with tremendous cries, all the Rākṣasas could find no bewilderment in Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: te śaraiḥ kṣatasarvāṅgā bhīmasenabhayārditāḥ bhīmam ārtasvaraṃ cakrur viprakīrṇamahāyudhāḥ
english: Their every limb cut by his arrows, tormented by fear of Bhīmasena, their great weapons scattered, they raised a cry of distress.

sanskrit: utsṛjya te gadāśūlān asiśaktiparaśvadhān dakṣiṇāṃ diśam ājagmus trāsitā dṛḍhadhanvanā
english: Casting aside their maces, spears, swords, javelins, and battle-axes, they fled toward the southern quarter, terrified of that firm-bowed hero.

sanskrit: tatra śūlagadāpāṇir vyūḍhorasko mahābhujaḥ sakhā vaiśravaṇasyāsīn maṇimān nāma rākṣasaḥ
english: There stood a Rākṣasa named Maṇimān, a friend of Vaiśravaṇa, broad-chested and mighty-armed, spear and mace in hand.

sanskrit: adarśayad adhīkāraṃ pauruṣaṃ ca mahābalaḥ sa tān dṛṣṭvā parāvṛttān smayamāna ivābravīt
english: Showing his authority and manliness, that man of great strength, seeing them turned in flight, spoke with something like a smile.

sanskrit: ekena bahavaḥ saṃkhye mānuṣeṇa parājitāḥ prāpya vaiśravaṇāvāsaṃ kiṃ vakṣyatha dhaneśvaram
english: "Defeated in battle by a single man — a mere mortal — when you reach the abode of Vaiśravaṇa, what will you say to the lord of wealth?"

sanskrit: evam ābhāṣya tān sarvān nyavartata sa rākṣasaḥ śaktiśūlagadāpāṇir abhyadhāvac ca pāṇḍavam
english: Having thus addressed them all, that Rākṣasa turned back; javelin, spear, and mace in hand, he charged at the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ vegena prabhinnam iva vāraṇam vatsadantais tribhiḥ pārśve bhīmasenaḥ samarpayat
english: As he came rushing with speed like a maddened elephant, Bhīmasena pierced him in the flank with three calf-toothed arrows.

sanskrit: maṇimān api saṃkruddhaḥ pragṛhya mahatīṃ gadām prāhiṇod bhīmasenāya parikṣipya mahābalaḥ
english: Maṇimān too, enraged, seized a great mace and with a mighty swing hurled it at Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: vidyudrūpāṃ mahāghorām ākāśe mahatīṃ gadām śarair bahubhir abhyarchad bhīmasenaḥ śilāśitaiḥ
english: Bhīmasena received that great and most terrible mace in the sky — blazing like lightning — with many stone-sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: pratyahanyanta te sarve gadām āsādya sāyakāḥ na vegaṃ dhārayām āsur gadāvegasya vegitāḥ
english: All those arrows meeting the mace were knocked back; driven by the mace's momentum, they could not check its force.

sanskrit: gadāyuddhasamācāraṃ budhyamānaḥ sa vīryavān vyaṃsayām āsa taṃ tasya prahāraṃ bhīmavikramaḥ
english: Understanding the practice of mace-combat, that valiant one of awesome prowess evaded his blow.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaktiṃ mahāghorāṃ rukmadaṇḍām ayasmayīm tasminn evāntare dhīmān prajahārātha rākṣasaḥ
english: Then, in that very interval, the shrewd Rākṣasa hurled a most terrible javelin with a golden shaft made of iron.

sanskrit: sā bhujaṃ bhīmanirhrādā bhittvā bhīmasya dakṣiṇam sāgnijvālā mahāraudrā papāta sahasā bhuvi
english: That roaring, blazing, supremely terrible weapon split Bhīma's right arm and suddenly fell to the ground.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho maheṣvāsaḥ śaktyāmitaparākramaḥ gadāṃ jagrāha kauravyo gadāyuddhaviśāradaḥ
english: Sorely pierced by the javelin, that great archer of immeasurable valor, that Kaurava skilled in mace-combat, seized his mace.

sanskrit: tāṃ pragṛhyonnadan bhīmaḥ sarvaśaikyāyasīṃ gadām tarasā so 'bhidudrāva maṇimantaṃ mahābalam
english: Roaring as he took up that mace of all-tempered iron, Bhīma swiftly charged at the mighty Maṇimān.

sanskrit: dīpyamānaṃ mahāśūlaṃ pragṛhya maṇimān api prāhiṇod bhīmasenāya vegena mahatā nadan
english: Maṇimān too, roaring, seized a blazing great spear and hurled it at Bhīmasena with tremendous force.

sanskrit: bhaṅktvā śūlaṃ gadāgreṇa gadāyuddhaviśāradaḥ abhidudrāva taṃ tūrṇaṃ garutmān iva pannagam
english: Shattering the spear with the tip of his mace, that master of mace-combat swiftly charged at him like Garuḍa upon a serpent.

sanskrit: so 'ntarikṣam abhiplutya vidhūya sahasā gadām pracikṣepa mahābāhur vinadya raṇamūrdhani
english: Leaping into the sky, that mighty-armed hero suddenly whirled his mace and, crying out, hurled it into the forefront of battle.

sanskrit: sendrāśanir ivendreṇa visṛṣṭā vātaraṃhasā hatvā rakṣaḥ kṣitiṃ prāpya kṛtyeva nipapāta ha
english: Like Indra's thunderbolt released by Indra himself, swift as the wind, it slew the Rākṣasa and, reaching the earth, fell like a deed accomplished.

sanskrit: taṃ rākṣasaṃ bhīmabalaṃ bhīmasenena pātitam dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni siṃheneva gavāṃ patim
english: All beings watched that Rākṣasa of terrible strength felled by Bhīmasena, as they might watch a lion bring down the lord of cattle.

sanskrit: taṃ prekṣya nihataṃ bhūmau hataśeṣā niśācarāḥ bhīmam ārtasvaraṃ kṛtvā jagmuḥ prācīṃ diśaṃ prati
english: Seeing him slain on the ground, the night-wanderers who survived raised a cry of anguish at Bhīma and fled toward the eastern quarter.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śrutvā bahuvidhaiḥ śabdair nādyamānā girer guhāḥ ajātaśatruḥ kaunteyo mādrīputrāv ubhāv api
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing the mountain's caves resound with many kinds of uproar, Ajātaśatru the son of Kuntī, and both sons of Mādrī as well —

sanskrit: dhaumyaḥ kṛṣṇā ca viprāś ca sarve ca suhṛdas tathā bhīmasenam apaśyantaḥ sarve vimanaso 'bhavan
english: — Dhaumya, Kṛṣṇā, the Brāhmaṇas, and all the companions — all were filled with dejection, not seeing Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: draupadīm ārṣṭiṣeṇāya pradāya tu mahārathāḥ sahitāḥ sāyudhāḥ śūrāḥ śailam āruruhus tadā
english: Entrusting Draupadī to Ārṣṭiṣeṇa, those great warriors — armed and valiant — then climbed the mountain together.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃprāpya śailāgraṃ vīkṣamāṇā mahārathāḥ dadṛśus te maheṣvāsā bhīmasenam ariṃdamam
english: Then, having reached the mountain's summit and looking about, those great chariot-warriors, those mighty bowmen, saw Bhīmasena the subduer of foes.

sanskrit: sphurataś ca mahākāyān gatasattvāṃś ca rākṣasān mahābalān mahāghorān bhīmasenena pātitān
english: And they saw the Rākṣasas — huge-bodied, mighty, most terrible — struck down by Bhīmasena, still twitching, their life-breaths departed.

sanskrit: śuśubhe sa mahābāhur gadākhaḍgadhanurdharaḥ nihatya samare sarvān dānavān maghavān iva
english: He shone splendidly, that mighty-armed hero bearing mace, sword, and bow, having slain all his foes in battle, like Maghavān having slain the Dānavas.

sanskrit: tatas te samatikramya pariṣvajya vṛkodaram tatropaviviśuḥ pārthāḥ prāptā gatim anuttamām
english: Then those sons of Pṛthā went to him, embraced Vṛkodara, and sat down there, having attained the most excellent of paths.

sanskrit: taiś caturbhir maheṣvāsair giriśṛṅgam aśobhata lokapālair mahābhāgair divaṃ devavarair iva
english: With those four great bowmen, supremely blessed like the guardians of the world, the mountain peak shone, as heaven shines with the best of gods.

sanskrit: kuberasadanaṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasāṃś ca nipātitān bhrātā bhrātaram āsīnam abhyabhāṣata pāṇḍavam
english: Seeing Kubera's abode and the Rākṣasas laid low, a brother addressed his brother, the son of Pāṇḍu seated there.

sanskrit: sāhasād yadi vā mohād bhīma pāpam idaṃ kṛtam naitat te sadṛśaṃ vīra muner iva mṛṣāvacaḥ
english: "Whether from rashness or from delusion, Bhīma, this sinful deed was done — it does not befit you, hero, like a false word does not befit a sage."

sanskrit: rājadviṣṭaṃ na kartavyam iti dharmavido viduḥ tridaśānām idaṃ dviṣṭaṃ bhīmasena tvayā kṛtam
english: "Those who know dharma know that what is hateful to kings must not be done; what is hateful to the thirty gods, O Bhīmasena, has been done by you."

sanskrit: arthadharmāv anādṛtya yaḥ pāpe kurute manaḥ karmaṇāṃ pārtha pāpānāṃ sa phalaṃ vindate dhruvam punar evaṃ na kartavyaṃ mama ced icchasi priyam
english: "He who disregards both wealth and righteousness and sets his mind on sin will surely reap the fruit of sinful deeds, O Pārtha. Do not act thus again, if you wish to please me."

sanskrit: evam uktvā sa dharmātmā bhrātā bhrātaram acyutam arthatattvavibhāgajñaḥ kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ virarāma mahātejās tam evārthaṃ vicintayan
english: Having spoken thus, that righteous-souled, greatly brilliant son of Kuntī, Yudhiṣṭhira — knower of the true nature of purpose — fell silent, contemplating that very matter.

sanskrit: tatas tu hataśiṣṭā ye bhīmasenena rākṣasāḥ sahitāḥ pratyapadyanta kuberasadanaṃ prati
english: Then those Rākṣasas who survived the slaughter by Bhīmasena assembled together and made their way back toward Kubera's abode.

sanskrit: te javena mahāvegāḥ prāpya vaiśravaṇālayam bhīmam ārtasvaraṃ cakrur bhīmasenabhayārditāḥ
english: They — swift and of great speed — reached the abode of Vaiśravaṇa and raised a mournful cry, tormented by fear of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: nyastaśastrāyudhāḥ śrāntāḥ śoṇitāktaparicchadāḥ prakīrṇamūrdhajā rājan yakṣādhipatim abruvan
english: Their weapons and arms laid down, exhausted, their garments soaked in blood, their hair dishevelled, O king, they spoke to the lord of Yakṣas.

sanskrit: gadāparighanistriṃśatomaraprāsayodhinaḥ rākṣasā nihatāḥ sarve tava deva puraḥsarāḥ
english: "Those Rākṣasas who fought with maces, iron clubs, swords, javelins, and lances — all your foremost attendants, O lord, have been slain."

sanskrit: pramṛdya tarasā śailaṃ mānuṣeṇa dhaneśvara ekena sahitāḥ saṃkhye hatāḥ krodhavaśā gaṇāḥ
english: "O lord of wealth, overrunning the mountain with swift force, a single mortal has slain the assembled host — the troops overcome by wrath."

sanskrit: pravarā rakṣasendrāṇāṃ yakṣāṇāṃ ca dhanādhipa śerate nihatā deva gatasattvāḥ parāsavaḥ
english: "The foremost among the lords of Rākṣasas and the Yakṣas, O master of wealth, O lord, lie slain, their life-breath departed, their vitality gone."

sanskrit: labdhaḥ śailo vayaṃ muktā maṇimāṃs te sakhā hataḥ mānuṣeṇa kṛtaṃ karma vidhatsva yad anantaram
english: "The mountain is taken, we have been routed, your friend Maṇimān is slain — a deed done by a mortal; ordain now what must follow."

sanskrit: sa tac chrutvā tu saṃkruddhaḥ sarvayakṣagaṇādhipaḥ kopasaṃraktanayanaḥ katham ity abravīd vacaḥ
english: Hearing this, the lord of all the Yakṣa hosts became intensely angry; his eyes reddened with rage, he spoke the word: "How?"

sanskrit: dvitīyam aparādhyantaṃ bhīmaṃ śrutvā dhaneśvaraḥ cukrodha yakṣādhipatir yujyatām iti cābravīt
english: Hearing of Bhīma's transgression for a second time, the lord of wealth, the lord of Yakṣas, grew wrathful and commanded: "Yoke up!"

sanskrit: athābhraghanasaṃkāśaṃ girikūṭam ivocchritam hayaiḥ saṃyojayām āsur gāndharvair uttamaṃ ratham
english: Then they yoked the finest chariot — resembling a mass of storm-clouds, towering like a mountain peak — with Gāndhārva horses.

sanskrit: tasya sarvaguṇopetā vimalākṣā hayottamāḥ tejobalajavopetā nānāratnavibhūṣitāḥ
english: Those finest of horses, endowed with every virtue, bright-eyed, possessed of brilliance, strength, and speed, adorned with manifold gems —

sanskrit: śobhamānā rathe yuktās tariṣyanta ivāśugāḥ harṣayām āsur anyonyam iṅgitair vijayāvahaiḥ
english: — resplendent as they were harnessed to the chariot, swift as if they would leap across all distance, they gladdened one another with gestures promising victory.

sanskrit: sa tam āsthāya bhagavān rājarājo mahāratham prayayau devagandharvaiḥ stūyamāno mahādyutiḥ
english: The blessed lord, king of kings, of great splendor, mounted that mighty chariot and rode forth, praised by gods and Gandharvas.

sanskrit: taṃ prayāntaṃ mahātmānaṃ sarvayakṣadhanādhipam raktākṣā hemasaṃkāśā mahākāyā mahābalāḥ
english: As that great-souled lord of all Yakṣas and of wealth set forth, those red-eyed ones, golden in hue, huge of body and mighty of strength —

sanskrit: sāyudhā baddhanistriṃśā yakṣā daśaśatāyutāḥ javena mahatā vīrāḥ parivāryopatasthire
english: — armed, swords girded, ten hundred thousand Yakṣa heroes with great speed surrounded and attended him.

sanskrit: taṃ mahāntam upāyāntaṃ dhaneśvaram upāntike dadṛśur hṛṣṭaromāṇaḥ pāṇḍavāḥ priyadarśanam
english: The Pāṇḍavas, their hair bristling with joy, beheld that great and pleasing lord of wealth approaching them nearby.

sanskrit: kuberas tu mahāsattvān pāṇḍoḥ putrān mahārathān āttakārmukanistriṃśān dṛṣṭvā prīto 'bhavat tadā
english: Kubera, for his part, seeing the mighty-souled sons of Pāṇḍu, those great chariot-warriors with bows drawn and swords in hand, was well pleased.

sanskrit: te pakṣiṇa ivotpatya gireḥ śṛṅgaṃ mahājavāḥ tasthus teṣāṃ samabhyāśe dhaneśvarapuraḥsarāḥ
english: They — swift as birds taking flight from a mountain peak — stood in close proximity to the Pāṇḍavas as the vanguard of the lord of wealth.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ hṛṣṭamanasaṃ pāṇḍavān prati bhārata samīkṣya yakṣagandharvā nirvikārā vyavasthitāḥ
english: Then, O Bhārata, looking upon him whose mind was glad toward the Pāṇḍavas, the Yakṣas and Gandharvas stood by composed and unperturbed.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś ca mahātmānaḥ praṇamya dhanadaṃ prabhum nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca dharmaputraś ca dharmavit
english: And the great-souled Pāṇḍavas — Nakula, Sahadeva, and the son of Dharma who knows dharma — having bowed to the lord who bestows wealth —

sanskrit: aparāddham ivātmānaṃ manyamānā mahārathāḥ tasthuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve parivārya dhaneśvaram
english: — those great chariot-warriors, feeling themselves as though they had offended, stood with palms joined in reverence, all surrounding the lord of wealth.

sanskrit: śayyāsanavaraṃ śrīmat puṣpakaṃ viśvakarmaṇā vihitaṃ citraparyantam ātiṣṭhata dhanādhipaḥ
english: The master of wealth took his seat upon the Puṣpaka — that excellent, splendid couch-and-throne fashioned by Viśvakarman with its wonderfully adorned borders.

sanskrit: tam āsīnaṃ mahākāyāḥ śaṅkukarṇā mahājavāḥ upopaviviśur yakṣā rākṣasāś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: As he sat there, those huge-bodied, spike-eared, and swift Yakṣas and Rākṣasas by the thousands sat down around him.

sanskrit: śataśaś cāpi gandharvās tathaivāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ parivāryopatiṣṭhanta yathā devāḥ śatakratum
english: And hundreds of Gandharvas and likewise hosts of Apsarases stood in attendance surrounding him, even as gods attend upon Śatakratu.
